skill.name: get-available-resources
skill.description: Detects local CPU, GPU, memory, disk, and operating system details, then creates resource-based recommendations for scientific computing workloads.
skill.summary: Inventory local compute resources before planning intensive workloads.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The fixed-argument subprocess calls and Markdown backticks are legitimate resource detection and documentation patterns, with no shell interpolation, network transfer, or prompt injection. Two local risks remain: the script intentionally inventories host details, and its custom output path can overwrite an existing file.

remediation.issue: A custom output path is opened in write mode and can replace an existing file.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output to the working directory and require explicit confirmation before replacing an existing file.

remediation.issue: The generated report includes host and working-directory details.
remediation.suggestion: Make detailed OS, processor, and path fields optional, and create reports with owner-only permissions.

content.user_title: Assess Compute Resources Before Scientific Work
content.value_statement: Large scientific workloads can fail or underperform when hardware constraints are unknown. This skill inventories local resources and recommends suitable processing, memory, storage, and acceleration strategies.
actual_capabilities: Reports physical and logical CPU cores, architecture, processor details, and available frequency data.
Captures total, available, and used memory plus swap capacity.
Measures total, available, and used disk space for the working directory.
Detects NVIDIA, AMD, and Apple Silicon GPUs through platform utilities.
Identifies the operating system, release, machine architecture, and Python version.
Creates a local report with recommendations for parallelism, memory, storage, and GPU libraries.
limitations: The script requires the third-party psutil package.
GPU detection depends on supported vendor utilities being installed and available on PATH.
Measurements are local snapshots and can change immediately after detection.
A custom output path can replace an existing file because the report uses write mode.

use_cases.title: Plan Large Dataset Analysis
use_cases.description: Check memory and disk capacity before choosing in-memory or chunked processing.

use_cases.title: Select Model Training Hardware
use_cases.description: Identify available GPU backends and compatible acceleration libraries before training.

use_cases.title: Size Parallel Workloads
use_cases.description: Use detected CPU capacity to choose a conservative worker count for simulations or batch processing.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Detect the compute resources available in this project and summarize the main constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Data Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess local resources for processing a [dataset size] dataset, then recommend an in-memory or out-of-core approach.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Training Backend
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect available GPUs and memory, then recommend a backend and library for training [model type].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Resource-Aware Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inventory this system and design a workflow for [task] using safe worker counts, memory limits, storage strategy, and hardware acceleration.

output_examples.input: Check whether this machine can process a 40 GB dataset.
output_examples.output: Available memory is below the dataset size. Use chunked, out-of-core processing and monitor the reported disk capacity for intermediate files.

output_examples.input: Find the best acceleration option for model training.
output_examples.output: One NVIDIA GPU is available with CUDA support. Use a CUDA-enabled framework after confirming the model and batch fit available GPU memory.

output_examples.input: Recommend a worker count for a CPU simulation.
output_examples.output: The system has eight logical cores. Start with six workers, leave capacity for the operating system, and measure performance before increasing concurrency.

best_practices: Run detection immediately before a resource-intensive task because available memory and disk space change.
Review the report before applying recommendations to production or shared systems.
Use a new report filename or confirm replacement before selecting a custom output path.
anti_patterns: Do not treat snapshot measurements as guaranteed capacity for a long-running workload.
Do not assume a detected GPU backend proves every required library is installed.
Do not expose generated reports publicly without reviewing system and path details.

faq.question: What resources does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects CPU, memory, disk, GPU, operating system, machine architecture, and Python version details.

faq.question: Does the skill send resource data over the network?
faq.answer: No network behavior appears in the reviewed files. The script writes its report locally.

faq.question: Which dependency is required?
faq.answer: The script requires psutil. Other imported functionality comes from the Python standard library.

faq.question: Which GPU platforms are supported?
faq.answer: It checks NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, and Apple Silicon Metal using available platform utilities.

faq.question: Are the recommendations benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. They are threshold-based suggestions derived from current resource measurements, not workload-specific performance tests.

faq.question: Can I choose another report location?
faq.answer: Yes. Review the path first because write mode can replace an existing file at the selected location.
